thread:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Canary 'v2-opt' error rate spike detected (5xx rate x12 over baseline) — approx 3% traffic. Triggering page to #incidents.

sre-oncall: seeing the same. Error stacktrace points to decoder mismatch in runtime kernels.

alex: confirmed — CPU and GPU memory look normal, but latency tail and 5xxs align with sequence-length-dependent perf cliff.

maria: rolling traffic to 0% for that canary now. Using feature-flag kill switch `ff/route-v2-opt` to isolate.

alex: on it. flipping flag: 
```bash
./ff-toggle --env prod --flag route-v2-opt --value off --reason "canary 5xx spike"
```

deploy-bot: action logged: ff/route-v2-opt set to OFF by alex at 2355004380. Traffic drain initiated (target 0% over 60s).

product-eng: tagging customer-impacted services: embeddings, rerank API. CS: notify high-touch customers?

customer-success: please share rough impact numbers before we send comms.

maria: quick assessment: 3% global traffic past 10m. Error amplification concentrated in long-context queries >2048 tokens. Estimated affected requests ~0.9% of total prod requests last hour.

ops: can we do a manual rollback of the model variant on the canary hosts instead of flag? which is faster?

alex: flag flip already in progress, but I'll also prepare a rollback to v2-opt-legacy (previous working variant) just in case. Command below.
```bash
# trigger rollback on canary node pool
./deploy rollback --pool canary-v2 --to v2-opt-legacy --wait 120
```

sre-oncall: prioritize verification plan: 1) confirm flag off and traffic 0 -> check routing logs 2) run smoke sample against rerank/embeddings 3) validate metric regression absent 4) re-run canary with limited traffic if we need deeper debug.

deploy-bot: rollback job created: job_id=rb-2026-2355004450, targeting canary-v2 (3 pods). ETA ~2m.

alex: rollback finished on canary pool. Pod images now v2-opt-legacy. Logs: last 3 deploy logs show readiness probes passing.

maria: verifying smoke tests now. Running 100 synthetic queries including long-context samples.

product-eng: add a quick check for hallucination rate on rerank outputs (recent regressions noticed).

maria: smoke results: 100/100 success for embeddings, rerank latency back to baseline, no 5xx observed in test window. Sampled real production requests against the canary hosts (mirrored) returned healthy responses.

ops: routing logs show canary traffic dropped to 0.0% at 2355004409 after flag flip and stayed at 0.0% post-rollback.

customer-success: thanks — we'll prep an interim note: small % of customers may have seen errors; limited scope; rollback completed and systems stabilized. Draft incoming.

sre-oncall: next steps — leave ff/route-v2-opt OFF to avoid re-exposure until root cause triage. Start a dedicated postmortem board and assign root-cause to eng-ml.

alex: attaching quick logs snippet from canary pre-rollback: 
```
[2026-07-18T14:45:29Z] ERROR decoder.cpp: mismatch in kv-cache layout for attention layer 8 -> raise 500
[2026-07-18T14:45:29Z] TRACE request-id=abc123 input_seq=4096 tokens=4096 model=v2-opt
```

product-eng: noted. ENG-ML to repro in staging with long-context fuzzing. If we can reproduce, we'll try kernel fallback and quantization profile changes.

sre-oncall: handing off to oncall-night (ops) at 2355004700. Keep ff/route-v2-opt OFF. If traffic reappears or errors return, escalate to pagers.

ops: acknowledged. I (ops) will own monitoring through night and coordinate with eng-ml tomorrow.

customer-success: sending comms to affected customers now — short blurb indicating a transient canary issue, rollback applied, monitoring continues.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: incident_id=INC-2026-235500, severity=high (canary regression, limited customer impact), state=stabilized, owner=sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: closing immediate page. We'll open a follow-up thread for the postmortem and RCA. Good job team. :thumbsup:
